subject: IaC presubmit: provider pinning, Helm scoping & GitLab pre-merge runway
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeinfra.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeinfra.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Acme on-prem IaC presubmit and gating requirements

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for taking this on. We’re getting ready to onboard Redwood into our private VPCs next quarter and procurement asked us to collect a concrete "presubmit" checklist for our internal change board. At a high level we need: provider pinning (we run a tightly controlled provider mirror), Helm value scoping (no unscoped global overrides), and an explicit pre-merge pipeline that runs a non-destructive staging deploy + connectivity smoke tests.

I attached a rough topology and our compliance matrix for reference (acme-privstack-topo.png). Can you propose a short checklist and the pipeline jobs you’ll expect to see so we can check them off in our change board?

Timeline: procurement prefers all evidence locked down by Jun 9 so the contract can clear. Happy to sync over a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Platform Engineering
Acme Infra Solutions

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Acme on-prem IaC presubmit and gating requirements

Jordan — thanks for the topo and the timeline. Looping in Marissa (compliance/product owner), Karthik (infra runtime lead) and Neha (security evidence). Below is a concise presubmit checklist we’ll use; I’m attaching a presubmit template you can drop into your repo (iac-presubmit-template.md).

Proposed short presubmit checklist (we’ll turn these into MR gating jobs):
- Provider pinning: lock Terraform providers in provider_constraints.tf and validate against our provider mirror; disallow > patch-level drift.
- Module provenance: every third-party module must have signed artifact references or be vendored into our private registry.
- Helm value scoping: require a values.schema.yaml and no global overrides that enable elevated privileges; run helm lint + schema validate.
- Non-destructive staging: pre-merge pipeline runs an infra-assert job that applies to an ephemeral staging namespace (namespaced resources only) using TF plan + apply with auto-destroy.
- Connectivity smoke: run a scripted smoke test that validates control-plane <-> data-plane routability (TCP handshake to known service ports) and KV cache accessibility.
- Secrets & KMS: explicit KMS key alias used in values; no plaintext secrets in Helm/Terraform.
- Proofpack evidence: produce proofpack entries (terraform plan output, helm lint artifacts, smoke test logs) zipped and uploaded to the MR.

Action items:
1) Karthik — can you list the MR jobs you want in GitLab for provider mirror validation and the ephemeral staging apply?
2) Neha — requested evidence format and retention for proofpack (we have an existing template but confirm).
3) Jordan — can you confirm the staging environment we’ll use (namespace prefix + node pool constraints) and whether the mirror supports provider plugin versions.

I attached the presubmit template. We can also do a 30m call Monday.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: iac-presubmit-template.md (text/markdown)

Thanks — quick technical notes and proposed pipeline jobs below.

Provider pinning:
- We expect a provider_constraints.tf checked into the root module with explicit version constraints (example: provider_registry/hashicorp/aws = "~> 4.38.0").
- Our recommended enforcement: pre-merge job provider-validate runs terraform providers lock -input=false and compares .terraform.lock.hcl to a golden lockfile stored in the repo (or fetched from your mirror). Fail MR if new provider checksums are introduced without an exception label.
- If your mirror requires a specific binary layout, provide a minimal provider-mirror-setup job that validates the mirror endpoint and returns a 200 + provider manifest.

Helm scoping & values:
- Require values.schema.json (or yaml) validated by helm schema-validation plugin. Add helm-lint job that runs helm template + kubeconform against schema.
- Disallow clusterRole creation by default; any workload requiring elevated privileges must present a short justification doc in MR.

Ephemeral staging & connectivity smoke:
- introduce jobs: tf-plan-staging, tf-apply-ephemeral (auto-destroy), smoke-connectivity.
- smoke-connectivity runs from a lightweight test pod and verifies TCP handshakes to ports 9090/8000 and S3-compatible endpoint used for artifact store. Also verifies that the KV cache endpoint returns a 200/OK on /healthz.

Secrets & KMS:
- secret-scan job (trufflehog or similar) and kms-assert job that validates the Terraform providers/kms key alias mapping.

Artifacts & proofpack:
- proofpack job zips plan.json, helm-lint.log, smoke.log and uploads to MR artifact storage and our compliance S3 bucket with a signed object key.

I can draft the .gitlab-ci.yml job stubs and push a sample MR to the Redwood iac repo by EOD Tuesday.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer

Jordan / team — a few compliance expectations I want on the record so procurement has what they need:

- Proofpack minimum: tf plan (redacted), helm lint + schema validation output, smoke test logs, and a signed manifest of third-party modules.
- Retention: evidence for the initial change retained for 180 days; longer retention negotiable for regulated workloads.
- KMS + audit: KMS key usage must be auditable; if you use a customer-managed HSM, provide a key rotation policy.
- Rollback: pre-merge gating must include a dry-run rollback verification (for example, a successful destroy plan that does not error for namespaced resources).

I’m attaching the compliance checklist spreadsheet we’ll use to mark items (compliance-proofpack-checklist.xlsx). If procurement needs an SLA exception (e.g., longer retention), flag it early so I can loop Legal.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful and aligns with what procurement asked for. Quick replies to outstanding questions:

- Staging env: use namespace prefix acme-redwood-stage- and the smaller shared node pool (np-small-1). That node pool disallows privileged containers by default and matches our change board safety posture.
- Provider mirror: yes, we support the provider mirror endpoint and can host a golden .terraform.lock.hcl for the initial rollout. I’ll attach the mirror manifest to the MR when we open it.
- Timeline: We’ll aim to open a scaffold MR with provider_constraints.tf, values.schema.yaml, and a smoke test stub by Jun 6. Procurement is copied and will add contract-level checklist items; they may ask for the compliance spreadsheet entries to be linked from the MR.

I’ll wait for the sample .gitlab-ci.yml from Karthik and then schedule a Friday change-board preview if needed.
